question: What is the primary function of tele-nursing in modern healthcare?

options.A: Replacing all face-to-face hospital visits permanently
options.B: Manufacturing digital medical devices for home use
options.C: Automating surgical procedures in rural clinics
options.D: Delivering nursing care through information and communication technologies

explanation: Tele-nursing specifically uses technology to provide, manage, and coordinate nursing services across distances. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: How does tele-nursing primarily benefit patients living in remote or underserved areas?

options.A: By providing continuous access to clinical expertise without long travel
options.B: By eliminating the need for any prescription medications
options.C: By guaranteeing complete immunity from chronic illnesses
options.D: By replacing community health extension workers entirely

explanation: Remote patients gain regular contact with healthcare providers, bypassing the physical burden of traveling to distant urban facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which tele-nursing model involves real-time interactions such as live video calls?
explanation: Synchronous models require the nurse and patient to interact simultaneously in real time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: A nurse reviews a blood glucose log sent via email by a patient three hours earlier. What model of care does this represent?
explanation: Store-and-forward or asynchronous methods involve transmitting data for review at a later, non-immediate time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is an example of a specialized peripheral device used in tele-nursing?
explanation: Digital and Bluetooth-enabled monitoring devices allow biometric data to be captured and transmitted for virtual review. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why is software interoperability important in digital health infrastructure?

options.A: It reduces the cost of manufacturing mobile smartphones
options.B: It ensures different digital systems can share patient data seamlessly
options.C: It eliminates the need for any electricity or internet connection
options.D: It automatically diagnoses rare genetic disorders

explanation: Interoperability allows diverse platforms to communicate effectively, preventing data silos and fragmented care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which regulatory body in Nigeria oversees professional nursing practice and standards?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria regulates professional conduct, licensing, and standards for nurses in the country. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is a primary ethical obligation when conducting virtual nursing consultations?

options.A: Sharing patient login credentials with family members freely
options.B: Recording all sessions without explicit patient knowledge
options.C: Maintaining strict confidentiality of transmitted health information
options.D: Publishing patient case studies on public social media platforms

explanation: Protecting patient privacy and securing digital health records are fundamental ethical duties in tele-nursing. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: What skill becomes especially vital when conducting clinical evaluations through virtual video platforms?

options.A: Keen visual observation and structured questioning
options.C: Direct physical palpation of deep abdominal organs

explanation: Because physical touch is absent, nurses must depend heavily on visual assessments and precise verbal communication. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h5)

question: How can a nurse successfully assess a patient's respiratory rate during a video consultation?

options.A: By guiding the patient or caregiver to count chest rises while observing
options.B: By listening through a stethoscope connected via local Bluetooth
options.C: By checking the patient's electronic health record from the previous year
options.D: By estimating the rate based solely on the patient's age and diagnosis

explanation: Nurses instruct remote participants to assist with basic physical checks like observing respiratory movements on camera. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which condition is commonly monitored using tele-nursing remote tracking strategies?
explanation: Chronic illnesses like diabetes require ongoing monitoring and lifestyle management, making them ideal for tele-nursing applications. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)

question: A nurse monitoring a patient with heart failure via tele-health notices a rapid weight gain over two days alongside mild ankle edema. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled in-person clinic visit next month
options.B: Contact the patient to assess for worsening fluid retention and notify the physician
options.C: Tell the patient to stop all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Advise the patient to increase daily fluid intake to flush out toxins

explanation: Sudden weight gain in heart failure often indicates fluid overload, requiring prompt clinical follow-up to prevent decompensation. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a major infrastructural barrier to tele-nursing in many resource-limited settings?

options.A: Excessive availability of advanced surgical robots
options.B: Unreliable power supply and poor internet connectivity
options.C: Universal free access to high-end tablet computers
options.D: An overabundance of high-speed fiber-optic networks

explanation: Frequent electricity outages and weak network signals are primary obstacles to sustained digital healthcare delivery. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h7)

question: How can nurses address low digital literacy among elderly patients during a tele-health rollout?

options.A: By demanding that family members move into the hospital permanently
options.B: By refusing to provide care until the patient buys a new computer
options.C: By abandoning all digital tools and reverting entirely to paper letters
options.D: By involving community health workers to assist patients with device navigation

explanation: Community intermediaries help bridge the digital divide by guiding patients through virtual interactions. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h7)

question: Which competency is increasingly vital for modern nurses entering tech-enabled healthcare environments?
explanation: Modern nursing requires a strong grasp of health informatics to effectively utilize software, trackers, and AI tools. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h8)

question: What role will artificial intelligence tools likely play in future tele-nursing workflows?

options.A: Eliminating the need for patient consent in clinical research
options.B: Completely replacing the human judgment of professional nurses
options.C: Manually performing physical surgeries in remote villages
options.D: Assisting with automated triage alerts and patient data analysis

explanation: AI serves as a supportive tool to help prioritize patient needs and process large volumes of biometric data. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h8)
